newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Manila stocks sink, other Asia shares drop.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks sink, other Asia shares drop.

text.p: Philippine share prices plunged over five percent on Tuesday in the market's largest single day sell-off in two years, and stocks in other Asian markets were also dented by local factors.
Expectations of poor first quarter corporate earnings and fears of a crash in the property sector sparked the downturn in Manila.

At the close, the composite index had clawed back from the session's low of 2,691.43 to end 128.87 points, or 4.54 percent, lower at 2,708.44 points. The property stock index was off 101.58 points, or 7.31 percent, at 1,287.43.

The Philippine Central Bank said on Tuesday it had set a 20 percent limit on loan exposure of banks to the real estate sector, the first time such a cap had been imposed. The dismal profits outlook reflected disappointment over the latest results of Philippine Long Distance Telephone (PLDT), a key blue chip stock.
PLDT, the county's premier telecommunications provider, said on Monday its earning dropped 1.8 percent for the first three months of 1997 to 1.28 billion pesos, dragged down by redundancy costs.
Although analysts and company officials remained sanguine over the outlook for the full year results, the first quarter's numbers spooked an already nervous market.
"The selling is tainted with emotions. It's already beyond reason," said Rolly Pineda, a vice president at Tower Securities.

Jitters over property stocks also hit Indonesian shares, which fell 9.18 points, or 1.40 percent, to 647.35 points in early afternoon trade following profit-taking in shares of property firm Elang Realty
"A sudden surge of active profit-taking in Elang sent it (the market) down very quickly and prompted the exchange authorities to suspend trading of the stock," one broker said.

The Jakarta Stock Exchange suspended trading in Elang Realty after it had fallen over 30 percent in early trade on Tuesday. Last week rumours circulated in the market the company would launch a rights issue, boosting its share price.
Thai stocks were battered amid heavy selling, with the key index off 14.11 points, or 2.11 percent, to 658.37 points in afternoon trading.

Banks bore the brunt of selling on fears their profits could fall if further bank interest rate cuts occurred. Several major Thai banks cut key interest rates a modest 25 percentage points on Monday. But traders said the cuts were too small to stimulate the slowing economy.
Malaysia's stock market failed to be cheered by news of a 367.2 million ringgit trade surplus in February.
Stocks fell 10.39 points, or 0.97 percent, to 1,064.47 points by early afternoon.
"Where do you hide? People are trying to pick the bottom on the market," said Jonathan Duckett, an institutional dealer at Mohaiyani Securities.
Singapore shares also suffered from a slump in property counters on persistent talk of new government curbs in the sector. Selling by foreign institutions further hurt investor confidence.
The Straits Times Index was off 14.71 points, or 0.74 percent, at 1,982.08 by mid-session.
Elsewhere in Asia, the Tokyo stock market was closed for a Japanese holiday. On Monday, the key Nikkei average ended 57.51 points, or 0.31 percent, higher at 18,670.37.
Hong Kong stocks slipped in afternoon trade on caution ahead of U.S. economic numbers due later in the day. The Hang Seng index was down 28 points, or 0.23 percent, at 12,581.

South Korean shares closed slightly lower on profit-taking, with the composite index down 0.11 of a point at 704.05. Traders were marking time until the limit on foreign stockholdings is lifted to 23 percent from 20 percent on May 2.
Taiwan stocks closed 68.32 points, or 0.79 percent, lower at 8,592.44 as the market consolidated from its recent advance.
Australia's All Ordinaries Index closed up 17.4 points at 2,479.1, while New Zealand shares closed 8.91 points higher at 2,249.13.

In India, trading was subdued as the market waited to see if former finance minister P. Chidambaram's party would join the new government. Bombay's 30-share index was trading at 3,815.74, down 9.77 points, or 0.26 percent, in early trade.
In Pakistan, stocks swung higher on short-covering with the Karachi 100-share index up 3.76 points at 1,530.68 at midday.

Dhaka stocks edged higher in early trade following recent sharp losses on concerns of a collapse in the Bangladesh banking sector. The Dhaka Stock Exchange all-share price index closed 60.32 points down at 899.38 on Monday.
